reasoning: This workflow is part of a ticketing lottery system for FairTix, a platform positioning itself as anti-scalper ('tickets for fans, not bots'). When someone wins the lottery for event tickets, their information is added to a Google Sheet, triggering this workflow. It sends a winning notification email with purchase instructions and updates the sheet status. The email template reveals key business model details: transparent pricing with no hidden fees, 24-hour purchase window, and a 'Fair Queue' selection system. The workflow is currently inactive with 0 executions, suggesting it's either newly built, in testing, or part of a demo system. The sheet structure (ID, Name, Email, EventName, TicketPrice, Status) indicates a lottery management system tracking winners.
name: Lottery Winner Notification & Tracking
businessNarrative: This workflow notifies lottery winners they've been selected to purchase event tickets through FairTix's anti-scalping system. It reveals a business model focused on fairness and transparency - winners have 24 hours to complete purchases at fixed prices with no hidden fees. The automation tracks notification status in Google Sheets, suggesting manual lottery draws or another system determines winners upstream. This positions FairTix as a premium ticketing platform differentiating through ethical practices rather than just technology.
trigger: New lottery winner added to Google Sheets
dataFlow: Lottery winner details (name, email, event, price) enter from Google Sheets row additions. The workflow sends a branded HTML email notification and updates the source sheet with status code 200, timestamp, and email message ID for tracking delivery.

impact.reasoning: Direct revenue impact - each successful notification can lead to ticket purchase within 24 hours. Failed notifications mean lost sales and poor customer experience for lottery winners. The fair queue system is core to brand promise.
impact.failureScenario: Lottery winners don't receive notifications, miss their 24-hour purchase window, tickets go unsold or to wrong buyers. Damages trust in 'fair queue' promise and loses direct revenue from committed buyers.
impact.revenueConnection: Direct - each notification drives time-sensitive ticket purchase conversions

detectability.reasoning: Sheet updates provide audit trail, but no active monitoring visible. Team would only know about failures through customer complaints or manual sheet reviews.
detectability.evidence: Error workflow configured (oZy3vc0yli2xdR45) but no other monitoring. Status updates to sheet provide some tracking.
